about: CCwiki's reviewed corrections for deriving relations from the wiki's relations.json. The manifest does not record hardness regimes, scoped notions, refutations or per-direction equivalence classes; these entries supply them until it does. Every entry cites the wiki's own text in `cites`: a page, a section (null for the whole file, frontmatter included) and a quote copied verbatim from the page source, which scripts/derivations_reference.py --check-quotes checks. The prose (evidence, reason or note) is for people. Spec: plans/derivations.md section 2a and plans/relations-followups.md section 2.2; the review is plans/curation-review.md. Read by scripts/derivations_reference.py and by the Swift Derivation type; the corpus test fails if an id here no longer resolves.

refuted.text: AMYY25 (§4.1, Theorem 4.6, Claim 4.7) give a public-coin sampler that meets the pre-condition of the public-coin circular evasive LWE formulation HLL23 assume (AMYY25's Assumption 4.1) and breaks its post-condition. That formulation is therefore false, conditional on the base hardness the theorem assumes for its pre-condition, which contains LWE samples. This refutes that formulation only: not every evasive LWE variant, and not ABE for unbounded-depth circuits as such.
refuted.evidence: content/Assumptions/learning-with-errors.md:113, :260, :272. The attacked formulation, sampler class and theorem are the PR #9 audit's pointers into AMYY25 (§4.1, Assumption 4.1; Theorem 4.6, p. 29; Claim 4.7, p. 30); the wiki's 'is false' does not pin down the formulation (AMYY25's Assumption 4.1) or state the base-hardness premise (wiki ask ccw:content-circular-evasive-lwe-scope). A pre-condition that contains LWE samples cannot hold unless LWE with those parameters is hard, so the premise implies that much. What the premise is (LWE in which modulus and noise regime, or anything beyond LWE) neither the audit nor the wiki states, and CCwiki does not guess it: the sentence names the premise without stating it until that ask, which needs the paper, records it.

cites.quote: Public-coin [[#Circular evasive LWE|circular evasive LWE]], the assumption behind ABE for unbounded-depth circuits ([[HLL23 - Attribute-Based Encryption for Circuits of Unbounded Depth from Lattices Garbled Circuits of Optimal Size, Laconic Functional Evaluation, and More|HLL23]]; [[evasive-lwe-to-abe]]), is false: some sampler satisfies the pre-condition but not the post-condition — [[AMYY25 - Evasive LWE Attacks, Variants & Obfustopia|AMYY25]]
if standard LWE remains hard even when $\mathbf{P}$ is given in the clear (pre-condition), then it remains hard even when the short preimage $\mathbf{K}$ is given instead (post-condition)
It is false — [[AMYY25 - Evasive LWE Attacks, Variants & Obfustopia|AMYY25]]

quarantine.reason: ISIS hardness implying SIS hardness, the record's left-to-right direction, is stated without its parameters: the Statement says only that it holds under conditions on the column count and norm bound, and gives neither the inequalities, the distributions nor a proof or reference. Read at fixed parameters it is false: with q = 2, m = 1, n = λ and β = 2, the vector z = 2 solves SIS, while a uniform ISIS target lies in the span of the single column with probability at most 2^(1−n). That refutes only an unrestricted fixed-parameter reading, not a correctly parameterized equivalence. Quarantined until the conditions and a proof or reference are recorded; the other direction, SIS(n, m, q, √(β²+1)) hard ⇒ ISIS(n, m−1, q, β) hard, is still used.

red-isis-inhomogeneous-sis-to-sis.note: SIS => ISIS (right to left) is the Sketch's fully black-box reduction, SIS(n, m, q, sqrt(beta^2 + 1)) hard => ISIS(n, m - 1, q, beta) hard: write a SIS instance as A = [A' | a]; one ISIS-oracle call on (A', a) returns z' with A'z' = a (mod q) and |z'| <= beta, and (z', -1) is a nonzero kernel vector of A of norm at most sqrt(beta^2 + 1). It takes the record's class. ISIS => SIS (left to right) is quarantined (quarantine entry); 'unstated' here claims nothing for it. Neither node carries the parameters, and CCwiki tracks none (R13).

cites.quote: One direction is immediate: if SIS is hard for $(n, m, q, \sqrt{\beta^2 + 1})$, then ISIS is hard for $(n, m - 1, q, \beta)$.

Write a SIS instance as $\mathbf{A} = [\mathbf{A}' \mid \mathbf{a}]$; then $(\mathbf{A}', \mathbf{a})$ is a uniform ISIS instance, and one ISIS-oracle call returning $\mathbf{z}'$ with $\mathbf{A}'\mathbf{z}' = \mathbf{a} \pmod q$ and $\|\mathbf{z}'\| \le \beta$ gives the nonzero kernel vector $(\mathbf{z}', -1)$ of $\mathbf{A}$, of norm at most $\sqrt{\beta^2 + 1}$.

red-rsa-to-fac-dlo24.note: RSA => FAC (left to right) is the ordinary fact that RSA hardness implies factoring hardness on the same modulus distribution, recorded fully black-box in the standard model as red-rsa-to-fac-rsa78; this record's model 'other' only under-claims it here. FAC => RSA (right to left) is DLO24's theorem, and only in its generic-RSA experiment with preprocessing (DLO24, Definition 28): the advice is fixed before the modulus is sampled, not computed from it as the Statement says, and the online adversary works on the encoded challenge through the model's generic interface, which also permits a non-generic intermediate computation on it, so the model is not only ring operations and equality tests (Definitions 15 and 16, Theorem 12). Its class 'free' holds inside that experiment only: the requires entry on the reverse direction makes every use of it conditional on it, and the model 'other' scopes what follows. Corrections: wiki ask ccw:content-dlo24-preprocessing.

requires.evidence: Statement: 'any such RSA adversary converts into a factoring adversary with polynomially related online complexity and polynomially longer advice'. So FAC => RSA takes factoring hardness against adversaries with preprocessing advice, which the fac node, whose adversary A(1^lambda, N) gets no advice, does not state, and gives RSA hardness against generic adversaries with preprocessing only. Per the PR #9 audit, DLO24's Definition 28 fixes the preprocessing from the security parameter and the random encoding before the modulus and challenge are sampled; the Statement's 'unbounded preprocessing on n' would let the advice contain a factor p of N = pq and make online factoring trivial (wiki ask ccw:content-dlo24-preprocessing). Nothing in the record concludes that notion of factoring, so this direction fires only on a given FAC, with idealised models included (model other), and the answer says what it assumes and concludes. RSA hardness implies factoring hardness (left to right, and red-rsa-to-fac-rsa78) is unaffected.

requires.notion: DLOG hard in Z_p^* (p prime, g a generator), where the Blum-Micali generator (the PRG) reads residues as integers: each x_i is the next exponent, and the output bit is [x_i >= (p-1)/2]
requires.notionMarkdown: DLOG hard in $\ZZ_p^*$ ($p$ prime, $g$ a generator), where the Blum–Micali generator (the PRG) reads residues as integers: each $x_i$ is the next exponent, and the output bit is $[x_i \ge (p-1)/2]$
requires.evidence: Statement: 'If DLOG is hard in Z_p^* (p prime, g a generator), the Blum-Micali generator is a PRG: ... it iterates x_{i+1} = g^{x_i} mod p and outputs at each step the bit [x_i >= (p-1)/2]'. The recurrence feeds each residue back as an integer exponent and the predicate compares residues by their integer order: an interface of the prime field Z_p that an arbitrary cyclic group's encoding does not supply. So DLOG derived from CDH, DDH or BDH, which lives in their own group, does not meet it. The rationale's 'uses only the group operation' is inaccurate (wiki ask ccw:content-bm84-rationale). DDH => PRG is still derived without BM84 (ElGamal, IL89, HILL99). CDH => PRG is not: it awaits a DLOG => OWF edge on the same group family (wiki ask ccw:missing-edge-dlog-to-owf), which with OWF => PRG (HILL99) would give it without BM84.

requires.evidence: Statement: 'in the OT-hybrid model every two-party functionality can be computed with unconditional security against malicious parties'. The proof substitutes a real OT for the ideal one, which needs OT secure against malicious parties, and in the stand-alone, static setting of the conclusion that means simulation-based security against a static malicious adversary: the OT page's game-based malicious definitions 'do not capture all malicious-sender attacks', so they would not do either. The OT page's definitions are semi-honest (oblivious-transfer.md:107), and EGL's OT is semi-honest. DMO00 is accepted on its Statement that non-trivial single-server PIR 'is therefore complete for secure two-party and multi-party computation', a claim about malicious security, so it includes upgrading the OT its PIR gives to security against malicious parties (by a semi-honest-to-malicious compiler: GMW87's, which uses one-way functions, or Haitner's fully black-box one); the page states the conclusion, not the upgrade (wiki ask ccw:missing-edge-ot-semi-honest-to-malicious). Semi-honest OT reaches malicious OT by Haitner's compiler (Hai08, Theorem 2 and Corollary 2), which the wiki does not record; until it does, semi-honest OT => MPC is refused here. What Kil88 and GMW87 conclude is the weakened notion in weakens:red-ot-to-mpc-kil88.

requires.evidence: Statement: 'A PRP (KeyGen, Eval, Invert) over a domain D with |D| superpolynomial in lambda is an invertible PRF for the traditional (forward-oracle) game', with the O(q^2/|D|) switching-lemma term, negligible only then. The PRP page's syntax puts no bound on D. On D = {0,1}, P_k(x) = x XOR k for a uniform bit k is exactly a random permutation, so a perfect PRP; querying both points never finds a collision, while a random function has one with probability 1/2, so the forward game is lost with advantage 1/2. The forward switching gap is at most q(q-1)/(2|D|). LR88 meets the condition under LR88's own premise, a PRF on {0,1}^n with 2^n superpolynomial in lambda: its PRP is on {0,1}^{2n}, and its bound is negligible only then (its Notes), so whenever LR88 gives a PRP at all, the domain is large. The prf node does not enforce that premise: the PRF page's syntax bounds neither domain nor range, and a PRF on a polynomial-size domain exists unconditionally (the key is a whole random table). CCwiki accepts LR88 relative to its own theorem; a large-domain PRF hypothesis for LR88 is proposed with the PRP rows of wiki ask ccw:node-hypothesis-regimes. sPRP => PRP does not meet the condition: a strong PRP may have a small domain too. The weakened conclusion is weakens:red-prp-to-invertible-prf.
